newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Cairns Group to discuss plan of action in Brazil.
newsitem.headline: Cairns Group to discuss plan of action in Brazil.

text.p: The Cairns Group of 15 agricultural exporting countries will hold its annual ministerial meeting on June 5-6 in Rio de Janeiro to prepare the ground for the next set of world trade talks, officials said.

Under the World Trade Organisation (WTO) Agriculture Agreement, further multilateral negotiations on agriculture are to begin by the end of 1999 which Group members hope will result in greater liberalisation of world farm trade.
"The main objective is to plan for the events occurring over the next two years," said Jose Graca Lima, head of the economics department at Brazil's Foreign Ministry.
"We aim to find a line of action that will deeepen the process of liberalisation, better said, reform, of agriculture," he added.

This week's meeting will concentrate on "analysis and exchange of information that will lead to the next round of negotiations on agriculture," said Nestor Osorio, Colombia's ambassador to the WTO and Cairns Group member.
The main goal of the Group is the "elimination of subsidies and all measures which are market distortions", added Osorio who is also the current chairman of the WTO's Committee on Agriculture.

As well as looking ahead to 1999, Group members will assess the results of the Uruguay Round global trade talks completed in 1994. The Group was largely responsible for the creation of a framework for farm trade reform in the Round.
"We are at a mid-point," said Charles Mott, Australia's ambassador to Brazil.
"It is a bit early to speculate on the nature of the strategy for going forward...But the Group has always worked for greater liberalisation of trade in agriculture," he added.
One of the Group's main concerns is the high level of subsidies in the European Union (EU), officials said.

At the first WTO ministerial conference in December last year, the EU battled with the US and Cairns Group countries over the wording of a statement on agriculture which some saw as a rehearsal for the even tougher bargaining expected in 1999.
Formed in 1986, the Cairns Group operates under Australian leadership on an informal basis without disciplinary procedures or strict rules and takes a consensual approach to decision-making.
Its members range from Thailand to Uruguay and account for about 20 percent of the world's agricultural exports.
The Rio de Janeiro meeting will be the first in which Paraguay participates as a full member, officials said.
